subject: Re: AcmeBank - Region pinning & data residency Qs
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: John Peterson <john.peterson@acmebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T16:15:00-07:00
Subject: AcmeBank — Region pinning & data residency follow-up

Hi John — great call today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Goal: Ensure sensitive customer PII and model traces remain in-region (US) while providing predictable failover options.
- Action items agreed: 1) Clarify backup/replication behavior and encryption at-rest/in-transit; 2) Confirm logging content (are request/response logs stored and do they contain PII?); 3) Outline cross-region failover options and expected RTO/RPO; 4) Follow up on private deployment options for stricter contracts.

Answers & immediate notes: 
- Default behavior: Redwood stores customer data and backups in the pinned region by default. Cross-region replication is an opt-in feature for DR and warm-standby scenarios.
- Encryption: All stored data, snapshots, and backups are encrypted with customer-managed keys where requested (KMS/HSM integrations available).
- Logs: Request logs can be configured to redact or never persist full request/response bodies; we recommend redaction of any free-text inputs containing PII.
- Retention: Configurable per-customer—default log retention is 30 days; longer retention available for audit reasons.

Attachments: redwood-region-pinning-overview.pdf (high-level flow), redwood-soc2-snapshot.pdf (controls summary).

Next steps: 
1) Can you confirm the primary region (US-east / US-west) you want pinned for the initial PoC?
2) Do you require cross-region backups/replication or is in-region backups sufficient for now?
3) Are there specific retention windows for logs/audit traces beyond 30 days?

I’ll pull Marissa in on the follow-up to provide architecture-level detail and a short tech-deep dive if helpful.

Thanks,

Thanks Aditya — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our security/compliance team: 

1) Backups: When you say backups are stored in-region by default, does that include automated snapshot copies and periodic full backups? If we enable cross-region failover, are those backups copied to the failover region or only the active data plane?

2) Logs and PII: We need to be certain that request/response logs stored for debugging do not contain unredacted PII. Can you describe which fields are logged by default and whether we can opt to never persist request/response payloads?

3) Failover SLA: For the PoC we’d want a warm-standby in a second US region with an RTO target. Do you have a published SLA or typical RTO/RPO numbers for cross-region failover?

4) Backup retention & restores: Typical regulatory ask is 7 years for certain audit artifacts, but for this PoC we’re likely looking at 1 year. Can Redwood support configurable long-term snapshot retention?

We’re planning to recommend your solution to our infra and security leads — they might ask for an architecture diagram and a short call with Marissa to go deeper. 

-John
John Peterson

Subject: Re: AcmeBank — Region pinning & data residency follow-up

Appreciate the clear list, John. Answers inline below — Marissa will add technical detail in her note.

1) Backups: automated snapshots and full backups are by-default stored in the pinned region. If cross-region failover is enabled, snapshots can be replicated to the secondary region as an opt-in replication job. Replication is asynchronous; we can discuss RPO windows during the technical call.

2) Logs & PII: By default we persist operational logs (timestamps, request id, routing metadata) and limited telemetry for cost/usage. Request/response bodies are NOT persisted by default for hosted seats unless "debug logging" is enabled. For enterprise/private deployments we can set a policy to never persist request/response payloads or to run automatic redaction where certain fields are stripped.

3) Failover SLA: Our standard cross-region failover pattern is warm-standby with automated routing failover. Typical RTO is in the 5-15 minute range depending on model warmup and cache warming; RPO depends on replication frequency (configurable). We can include a dedicated Dedicated pool for guaranteed throughput and faster RTO if needed. Formal SLA terms would be part of the Dedicated/Private contract.

4) Retention: Long-term snapshot retention (1 year+) is supported. Snapshots are immutable and encrypted; we can set lifecycle policies to retain or purge snapshots per your compliance requirements.

Links: architecture diagram in the drive: https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-region-pinning-diagram

Proposed next step: Tech deep-dive with Marissa next week to go over replication cadence, KMS key flows, and a sample MAP. Are you available Tue/Wed next week?

Thanks,
Aditya
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-01T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AcmeBank — Region pinning & data residency follow-up

Hi John — Marissa here (Solutions Engineering). Following up with technical details and a short checklist so your security team can validate controls quickly.

Summary answers: 
- Backup & replication: Snapshots are taken at the storage layer and are encrypted with AES-256. By default snapshots remain in the primary region. If you opt into cross-region replication, snapshots are copied to the failover region; you can choose replication cadence (hourly/daily) which sets the RPO.

- On PII in logs: Redwood stores the following by default: request id, model id, token counts, latency, truncated error traces. Request/response payloads are not stored for hosted customers unless debug mode is explicitly enabled. For enterprise customers we offer: 
  - redaction pipeline (automated regex-based scrubbing),
  - field allowlists/denylists, or
  - never-persist policy enforced at the ingestion layer.

- Cross-region failover: We support two patterns: 
  1) Active-in-region + warm standby: secondary region has pre-provisioned capacity; failover routing is automated with an expected RTO of 5-15 mins (model warmup dependent).
  2) Active-active (for customers who need geo-low latency): replication of KV/prefix caches is more complex and usually self-hosted/private deployments are recommended for strict consistency.

- Backups & long-term retention: We can export encrypted snapshots to a customer-managed bucket for archive (S3/GCS) and/or set an immutable retention policy for up to 7 years. Restore tests can be scheduled as part of the onboarding MAP.

Sample items for your security questionnaire:
- SOC2 controls summary: attached (redwood-soc2-snapshot.pdf)
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, KMS integrations available
- Access: RBAC, audit logs, and support for customer-managed VPCs for Private deployments

Requested next steps: 
1) Please confirm: primary region (us-east-1 or us-west-2) and whether you want cross-region replication for PoC.
2) If you want, I can put together a 30-min technical demo next Tue/Wed and a short MAP with milestones for compliance sign-off.

If helpful I’ll also include a short sample config showing how to enable redaction and set snapshot retention.

Regards,
